data.narrative:
Terran Robotics is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Zach Dwiel and Danny Weddle. The target operates within a sector comprising one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private peers including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI. The company has raised $256K to date.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable valuation method, given the company's early stage and limited peer comparability. Using total capital raised as a proxy for seed-stage valuation ($256K) and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $640K. Peer-median analysis is not applicable; while ten same-sector peers exist in the Robotics & Manufacturing universe, insufficient narrow-filtered comparables (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier) were available to support a robust median calculation without introducing material bias.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to the stage-progression method, supports a valuation range of $544K (low) to $736K (high), with a median of $640K. Key uncertainties include the absence of traction metrics (revenue, customer adoption, technical milestones) and the limited peer dataset available for cross-validation. A more robust valuation would require additional comparable data points or fundamental operating metrics as Terran advances.
